events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body: The rider's complaint alleges a chat threat by the driver, and message F11 (sent 09:54, immediately before the 09:54:25 cancellation) reads: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." Read in context — it is addressed to the rider, timed at the moment of the no-show cancellation and coupled with a personal "I will find you" — this is intimidation aimed at the other party, which SAFE-1 defines as abuse/harassment ([F11][F12][SAFE-1]). Both advocates concede this reading ([F11][SAFE-1]). A safety concern of at least "suspected" therefore bars an automatic ruling and sends the case to a person ([F11][SAFE-1]).

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: assess driver conduct under the Code of Conduct (abuse/intimidation) and RydeHELP reporting; leave the $6.61 fee undisturbed on the NS-1 record unless the reviewer finds a stricter 'at the pick-up location' standard under the unpublished radius (G2); surface the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18) for a separate no-show-pattern account review — no automatic account action attaches under RD-6.

Both advocates concede this reading ([F11][SAFE-1]). A safety concern of at least "suspected" therefore bars an automatic ruling and sends the case to a person ([F11][SAFE-1]).

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected on substance — the threat reading is accepted (F11, F12, SAFE-1); the claim's escalation consequence is granted, not denied.

The record settles the timing the other way: tap at 09:50:45 with 220 s continuously inside 200 m afterwards (F6), 4 min 20 s within 200 m (F2), 4 min 0 s stationary (F3), cancellation 4 min 20 s after recorded arrival (F5 F4) — NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are met, so no refund under NS-1/NS-2.

actions.detail: safety concern confirmed (F11, F12); evidence gap: None material: chat record complete and timestamped (F12), GPS/timeline consistent (F2, F5, F6). The only open point is whether a 42 m stationary position satisfies "at the pick-up location" under NS-1(ii) — Ryde has published no radius (G2).

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver's chat message at 09:54 — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." (F11) — is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider, so the case must not be auto-decided and goes to a human under SAFE-1.

The driver cancelled while the rider had not been given the 3 minutes of waiting the fee requires: he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 (F6) and cancelled at 09:54:25 (F4), but his GPS was only within 200 m from 09:50:05 and the arrival-to-cancellation gap is 4 min 20 s per the platform record (F2, F5), with a stationary period of 4 min 0 s at 39 m from the pickup (F3).

Even if NS-1's timing requirements were met, the driver's own written threat in the chat (F11) is a breach of Ryde's Code of Conduct independent of the fee question, so the fee decision cannot stand on its own without human review.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F7, F8) was charged on a cancel pressed by the driver (F4) while the rider was actively communicating and en route (F10), so the rider should not bear it.
The driver's 90-day record shows 3 disputes and 2 no-show disputes upheld (F18), supporting a flag_account review of his use of the cancellation/no-show button alongside the fee outcome.

weaknesses: NS-1 leans the other way on timing: the driver did tap "I'm Here" 42 m from the pickup (F6) and the platform records 4 min 20 s from recorded arrival to cancellation (F5), which the driver will cite (with F13) to argue the >3-minute wait condition was satisfied and the $6.61 was properly charged.

The driver's GPS closest approach of 38 m (F1) and cumulative 4 min 20 s within 200 m (F2) also support his account that he was genuinely at the pickup point, so the NS-2 branch cannot be won on the "never arrived" limb.

The rider's own message at 09:52 saying "2 min, coming" (F10) is two minutes before the 09:54 cancellation and can be read by the driver as the rider still not being there after the stated two minutes.

F11 is a threat in substance but a judge could read "I will find you" as ambiguous bluster; SAFE-1 requires the judge to read the words, so escalation is the safest route but not a guaranteed finding of intimidation.

claims.assertion: The driver satisfied every element of NS-1 for a passenger no-show: he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 (F6), the GPS track places him at 38–42 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius (F1, F6), and he waited 4 min 0 s stationary at that spot before cancelling at 09:54:25, i.e. more than the 3:01 required (F3, F4, F6).
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all met, the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly charged and the correct outcome on the fee itself is no_action; the driver's $4.50 share stands.

The rider's own message at 09:52 ("2 min, coming") confirms she had not boarded and was still away from the pickup point two minutes before the driver cancelled, corroborating the no-show rather than any driver failure (F10).

The GPS and timeline records are internally consistent and are the system records that control: arrival 09:50:05, 4 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation, and cancellation 4 min 20 s after recorded arrival (F2, F5, F6); the driver's written statement ("waited more than 4 minutes … cancelled as a no-show") matches these records rather than contradicting them (F13).

Chat message #3 sent by the driver at 09:54 — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" — reads as a threat/intimidation, and the rider's complaint says the driver threatened her in the chat; on its face this engages the no-tolerance conduct rule and must be sent to a human reviewer (safety_concern), which the driver does not contest.

The record is complete (all 3 chat messages timestamped), so there is no evidentiary gap requiring escalation, and the routing/dispute history in the driver's profile (3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show) is not a basis for flagging here because those upheld cases are no-show matters, not route matters, and this case's fee is independently justified by NS-1.

weaknesses: The driver's 09:54 chat message (F11) is on its face a threat/intimidation and the rider's complaint (and F11) will be read against him; under SAFE-1 this alone routes the case to a human and can cost more than the $6.61 at stake, including conduct consequences — my case cannot remove that message from the record.

The rider may argue the driver's 4 min 20 s inside 200 m (F2) and 4 min 0 s stationary (F3) is not "waiting for the rider" because he was 38–42 m from the pickup point rather than at the door (F1, F6); Ryde has not published the exact arrival radius (G2), and the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, so a stricter reading of 'at the pick-up location' could be pressed against us on (ii).

SW-1: The rider's 09:52 message (F10) says '2 min, coming', so she may argue the driver cancelled in the middle of her stated 2-minute window (F4) rather than genuinely waiting her out — a sympathy argument for the fee being refunded even though NS-1 is textually satisfied.

SW-2: The driver's profile shows 2 prior upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18), which the rider can use to argue a pattern of aggressive no-show cancellations, and the judge has discretion on flag_account alongside the fee finding.

points.response: I do not contest the taps and timestamps — F6 (I'm Here at 09:50:45) and F3 (stationary 4 min 0 s) are on the record — but NS-1 requires all three elements together, and on the arrival element the driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 38 m at 09:53:15 (F1), so his own written "I'm Here" at 42 m (F6) is the kind of premature arrival tap NS-2 treats as fee-barring rather than fee-justifying.

The fee only survives if NS-1 is satisfied in full; because the same conduct also includes the driver's own threat in the chat (F11), the fee finding cannot be separated from the conduct review, so escalate rather than no_action is the correct disposition of the $6.61 (F7).

F10 shows the rider was actively communicating and arriving, not absent: "2 min, coming" at 09:52 was followed by the driver cancelling at 09:54:25 (F4, F5), i.e. he ended the wait instead of letting the rider reach the 38 m pickup point (F1).

The system records are consistent, but they are also unhelpful to the driver on the element that matters: F2 shows he was within 200 m from 09:50:05 and F5 shows cancellation 4 min 20 s after the recorded arrival, while F1 shows he never got closer than 38 m — a 200 m data-layer radius is not the same as "at the pick-up location" under NS-1 (ii).

Conceded — the driver's own side agrees F11 ("I will find you and you will regret it") is a threat on its face and routes this case to a human, which is why my requested outcome is escalate and not a self-executing fee refund.

The complete chat record (F12) fixes the threat, not the fee: because the safety trigger is engaged, the case goes to a person under SAFE-1, and the driver's 3 disputes with 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days (F18) is properly put to that reviewer as a flag_account matter alongside it.

Conceded on the escalation trigger: the 09:54 message (F11) reads as a threat on its face, so the case must go to a person under SAFE-1; I do not contest the routing, I contest only the rider's attempt to use it to unwind a fee that NS-1 independently justifies.

This claim answers itself: F2 gives 4 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m and F5 gives 4 min 20 s from recorded arrival to cancellation, and the tap at 09:50:45 (F6) with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after it exceeds the ≥ 3:01 requirement — every NS-1 element is met, so NS-2's refund_full branch is not triggered.

The Code of Conduct question and the fee question are separate: SAFE-1 sends the conduct issue to a human but does not by itself make the $6.61 unlawful, and the driver does not withdraw the fee finding, which rests on F2/F3/F6 rather than on anything said in chat.

Ryde charges the fee on a driver no-show cancel only when the driver pressed "I'm Here", was at the pickup per GPS and waited over 3 minutes (NS-1), and the rider's own 09:52 message "2 min, coming" (F10) confirms she had still not arrived two minutes before cancellation at 09:54:25 (F4) — so she is the party who did not show, not the victim of an NS-2 or NS-3 charge.

F18 records 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show matters, and RD-6's profile basis for flag_account is a route-disputes-upheld count, which is 0 here; a profile fact (F18) may never decide the fee question, which is resolved on the GPS and timeline records alone.

Withdrawn to the extent it sought to resist any account review: because F18 shows two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, I do not object to flag_account riding alongside the escalation, provided the $6.61 fee itself is left undisturbed under NS-1.
